name: MMEConversionFactorsExample
title: MME Conversion Factors Supplement Example
description: Example of an RxNorm code system supplement used to share configuration data, in this case the clinical conversion factors used to calculate Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME), as described in the CDC Opioid Prescribing Guideline. The supplement defines a conversion factor for each opioid ingredient in one of three ways: as a direct conversion factor for the ingredient, as a dose-form-specific conversion factor, or as a dose-quantity-ranged conversion factor. All conversion factors are in 'mg/d'. This example is based on the [CDCMMEClinicalConversionFactors](https://fhir.org/guides/cdc/opioid-mme-r4/CodeSystem-CDCMMEClinicalConversionFactors.html) code system supplement published in the CDC Opioid MME implementation guide.
purpose: Illustrates sharing configuration data (MME conversion factors) as properties defined in a code system supplement, so that the configuration can be distributed and versioned using the same artifact management infrastructure as the logic that uses it.
copyright: Conversion factors are derived from the CDC Opioid Prescribing Guideline, Copyright 2019+ Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). This material contains content from RxNorm, which is publicly available courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM).

property.description: Defines the conversion factor for a specific ingredient, when the conversion factor is the same for all dose forms and dose amounts for the ingredient. The value of this property will be the decimal representation of the conversion factor.

Defines the conversion factor for an ingredient when the conversion factor varies by the dose form of the medication. The value of this property will be a string of the form <dose-form-code>:<conversion-factor>[@<doses-per-day>], e.g. 970789:130, where '970789' is the RxNorm dose form code, and '130' is the decimal representation of the conversion factor. An example of a per-day conversion factor is fentanyl, 316987:7200@0.33333333, where 316987 is RxNorm dose form code, 7200 is the conversion factor, and 0.33333333 is the dosesPerDay, expressed as a decimal with a maximum of 8 digits after the decimal.

Defines the conversion factor for an ingredient when the conversion factor varies by the overall dose of the medication. The value of this property will be a string of the form <low-value>-<high-value>:<conversion-factor>, e.g. 1-20:4. Note that the low-value or high-value may be a wildcard '*' to indicate the range continues (e.g. '61-*:12' indicates the range is 61 or greater).
